title: POC sprint orchestra playbook
body:
Executive summary:

This playbook outlines a 6-week, engineering-led POC for a mid-size SaaS customer (ACME Inc.). It is intended for Solutions Engineering delivery partners and the customer engineering contact. Primary objective: validate a production-grade inference path for ACME's customer-support summarization pipeline with measurable latency and cost targets while proving integration steps for Dedicated and Private deployment modes.

Success metrics (must be measured during acceptance run):
- Functional: end-to-end summaries match baseline quality thresholds (ROUGE-L >= 0.78 on evaluation set).
- Performance: 95th percentile latency for the 2k-token summarization path under target load <= 250ms on Dedicated config; cold-start median <= 120ms.
- Cost: projected token-inference unit cost delta <= 30% vs baseline (internal estimate).
- Reliability: 99.5% of requests succeed under the defined load profile (50 concurrent sessions, 3x traffic burst).

Scope and exclusions:
- In scope: API integration, model variant selection, batching/caching config, basic observability dashboard, a single canary rollout test, and an integration lab with sample customer data (sanitized).
- Out of scope: full Private air-gapped install, enterprise SAML tweaks, long-term retention of logs beyond the trial, custom model training.

Stakeholders and roles:
- Solutions Lead: Maya Patel (owner)
- SE Implementation: Tom Reynolds (integration, runbooks)
- Inference SME: Lina Chen (runtime tuning, quant profiles)
- Customer Eng Contact: Diego Alvarez (ACME)
- SRE/Oncall: rotation from eng-sre (primary contact: sre-oncall@redwood.com)

High-level timeline (6 weeks)
Week 0 (pre-kickoff, 3 business days):
- Complete NDA and data sharing checklist (owner: Maya)
- Provision sandbox project and API keys (owner: Tom)
- Customer provides 3 anonymized example tickets + baseline summaries (owner: Diego)

Week 1 (kickoff + discovery):
- Kickoff workshop (90m) agenda: objectives, success metrics, infra constraints, SLAs, integration points.
- Run a discovery spike to confirm average and 95th percentile input lengths and distribution (Lina).
- Deliverable: discovery notes + recommended model family and initial config (doc).

Week 2 (integration + small-scale testing):
- Integrate Redwood API endpoints with ACME staging environment (Tom).
- Implement a minimal client wrapper to standardize retries and streaming handling (SE artifact).
- Run functional tests against sample data; capture quality metrics.

Week 3 (performance tuning and batching):
- Enable batching and KV prefix caching in staging. Test multiple batch sizes and quantify latency/cost tradeoffs (Lina).
- Introduce a canary policy: route 5% of traffic to tuned config.
- Deliverable: perf matrix + recommended default config.

Week 4 (scale test and observability):
- Execute load profile: sustained 50 concurrent sessions for 30 minutes, plus 3 sudden bursts at 2x the target rate. Capture p50/p95/p99 and error rates.
- Enable Redwood Console dashboards and link customer logs for the trial.
- Post-test retro to record anomalies and mitigations.

Week 5 (acceptance checks and runbook handoff):
- Run acceptance suite with blinded eval set for quality and regression checks.
- Finalize operational runbook: incident playbooks, fallback policies, model rollback step-by-step.
- Customer sign-off session scheduled end of week.

Week 6 (wrap and recommendations):
- Deliver handoff package: cost model, rollout plan to Dedicated/Private, open action items.
- Optional 2-week hypercare offer (terms to be discussed).

POC event checklist (quick):
- [ ] NDA complete
- [ ] Data sanitized and transferred
- [ ] Sandbox API keys provisioned
- [ ] Baseline metrics captured
- [ ] Canary policy validated
- [ ] Observability linked to customer dashboard

Acceptance criteria (concrete):
- Quality: automated eval passes: test suite accuracy >= baseline -5% relative drop.
- Latency: p95 <= 250ms under the specified load profile.
- Cost: estimated per-1M-token inference cost <= 1.3x baseline.
- Ops: runbook covers rollback, model variant fallback, and alerting thresholds.

Risk register and mitigations:
- Data sensitivity: if customer data contains PHI, escalate to security; require Private deployment or data masking steps.
- Unexpected latency spikes: have a fallback routing policy to a cheaper low-latency model and enable autoscaling buffer (2 GPU burst).
- Model quality regression: maintain an A/B test and immediate rollback to last-known-good model via model pinning.
- Integration blockers: reserve two 2-hour deep-dive windows with ACME's infra team during Week 2 to unblock networking/egress issues.

Task tracker (example rows) - to be synced to JIRA:
- SE-101: Provision sandbox project and keys (owner: Tom; due: Week0 day2)
- SE-102: Discovery spike and input-length histogram (owner: Lina; due: Week1 day3)
- SE-110: Implement client wrapper and retry logic (owner: Tom; due: Week2 day4)
- SE-120: Batching experiments and perf matrix (owner: Lina; due: Week3 day5)
- SE-130: Load test execution and retro (owner: Maya; due: Week4 day3)
- SE-140: Acceptance runbook and handoff docs (owner: Maya; due: Week5 day5)

Workshop playbook (kickoff and two technical deep dives):
- Kickoff (90m)
  - Intros + objectives (10m)
  - Success metrics and acceptance criteria review (10m)
  - Architecture walkthrough: customer data path, network diagram, auth, secrets (20m)
  - Integration checklist + responsibilities (15m)
  - Risks and mitigations quick sync (10m)
  - Next steps and calendar alignment (25m)

- Deep-dive 1 (networking and sandbox integration, 60m)
  - Confirm egress rules, NAT, firewall rules, routing to Redwood endpoints
  - Validate sample request/response and tokenization discrepancies

- Deep-dive 2 (observability and performance, 60m)
  - Dashboard walkthrough, alert thresholds, and export of traces/logs
  - Review KV cache hit-rate expectations and traces for cold-starts

Decision log (template entries):
- 2025-02-12: Model family chosen: llama-like open variant 70B quantized (decision by Lina)
- 2025-02-20: Canary traffic set to 5% then 20% after perf validation (decision by Maya + ACME)

Unresolved questions / open items:
- Customer asks whether SAML will be required for long-term Dedicated deployment (owner: Maya)
- Confirm whether ACME needs log redaction beyond our standard retention (owner: Diego)

Runbook excerpt (incident path):
- Alert triggers: p95 latency > 350ms for 5m OR error rate > 2% for 3m.
- First responder: SE oncall triage, run health-check: model server CPU/GPU load, queuing, batch sizes.
- Escalation: route 10% traffic to fallback model variant and open a postmortem if >15m.

Cost estimate (back-of-envelope):
- Sandbox testing (dev hours + ephemeral infra): ~$2k–$4k for 6 weeks
- Projected monthly Dedicated cost at target capacity: ~$18k–$25k depending on quantization profile and average token rate

Handoff deliverables (end of POC):
- Integrated client wrapper and sample app repo link (GitHub)
- Performance matrix and recommended default config
- Operational runbook and rollback steps
- Cost model and next-phase rollout recommendation

Appendix: useful links and references
- Example JIRA board: JIRA-8072
- GitHub artifacts: https://github.com/redwood-inference/poc-scripts/pull/58
- Slack channel: #poc-acme-activation

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the Week 3 batching experiments narrow: test 1, 4, 8 batch sizes only. Avoid too many variables.
- Prep a short demo script that shows both streaming and final summary flows.
- Remind ACME to provide a small tagged set for blind eval (20 examples).

End of playbook.
